correctness.rationale: Independently split the junction-crossing n coordinates from the two unchanged tails (RESULT.md:25–55). For the forward shift the positive tail contributes its norm as one scalar alongside n crossing coordinates; the distorted block is exactly a comparison of scalar l_p^(n+1) against l_2^(n+1). The backward shift reverses that comparison. Untouched negative coordinates contribute an identical square on the respective numerator and denominator. Equal-magnitude crossing coordinates and one extra positive coordinate attain the increasing norm, and one untouched negative coordinate attains each contractive norm 1. This also proves boundedness and bounded invertibility. Polynomial growth in both directions confines the spectrum to the unit circle, and phase conjugation plus nonemptiness proves equality. Uniform norm equivalence would make both directions power bounded for a surjective isometry, which is impossible for p!=2. The ordinary bilateral l_p shift is indeed a different isometric extension. No numerical optimization is required. The equality-witness description in the verification section should be understood as referring to the growing bounds: a negative single-coordinate vector suffices in the norm-one cases.
